back: The organised teaching process that develops motor skills, physical qualities, health and knowledge about exercise.
Strength, speed, endurance, flexibility and agility (coordination).
Regular activity, rational nutrition, enough sleep and rest, hygiene, no harmful habits, stress control.
Activity and consciousness, visual demonstration, systematic training, gradual increase of load, individual approach, accessibility.

front: Common causes of injuries in PE
back: No warm-up, wrong technique or too heavy load, bad clothes or shoes, breaking discipline, poor equipment or floor, training while ill.
First aid for sprains and bruises: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation. Tell the teacher; see a doctor if pain is strong.
Regular observation of your body's state and its reaction to exercise, usually recorded in a self-monitoring diary.
Subjective: what you feel (mood, sleep, appetite, well-being). Objective: what you measure (pulse, blood pressure, weight, lung capacity).
Two fingers on wrist or neck; count 10 s × 6 or 15 s × 4. Normal resting adult rate is about 60–100 beats/min.
Paleness or strong redness, heavy sweating, fast irregular breathing, unsteady movements, slow reactions. Stop and tell the teacher.
The largest volume of air you can breathe out after the deepest breath in; measured with a spirometer.
Measuring the body: height, weight, chest circumference (rest, inhale, exhale) and hand-grip strength.
Weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². Below 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30+ obesity.
Hand-grip strength (kg) ÷ body weight (kg) × 100%. Shows strength relative to body weight.
10–15 minutes of 8–12 light general exercises after waking, ordered from top to bottom, ending with walking and breathing.
Choosing your own morning gymnastics complex and demonstrating it (week 7).
Kazakh national game: players shoot a sheep's knucklebone (asyk) at a row of asyks to knock them out.
Kazakh national horseback team game: riders fight for a goat carcass and carry it to the goal.

front: Phases of the standing long jump
back: Preparation (arm swing, knees bent), take-off from both feet, flight (knees to chest), landing on both feet leaning forward.

front: How is the PE credit graded?
back: Differentiated credit from practical work and two midterm controls (weeks 7 and 15). Normative values are not in the syllabus: ask the teacher.
